raw_response:
I’m farming only 5 mu, so I can’t take big risks. Same as most years, I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation on all 5 mu. Wheat and maize together are the safest for me: wheat gives steady grain, and maize follows right after, so the land doesn’t sit idle. The extension guy talks about exact rates, but on my land I still go mostly by what I saw before. If I cut fertilizer too much, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than saving a little cash. But I also can’t spend too much at once because some people in my family work outside and cash use is tight. So this year I’ll do a moderate plan: enough base fertilizer for wheat, one topdress at jointing if the color is not good, then maize planted quickly after wheat harvest with simpler field prep. Since I have well water, I’ll keep irrigation for the key stages, but not too many times because pumping costs money.
